subject: Valora incident: scope for retained logs & sample delivery
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@valora.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops@valora.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Valora — post-incident log window and sample request

Jonas,

Thanks again for the support during the outage this morning. Valora's IR team is assembling a timeline and needs clarification on two items so we can close our incident report and satisfy our auditors:

1) Exact retention window: for the affected ingress and routing components, how long will you retain the full request/response payloads and the associated lower-level kernel logs after the incident window closes? We need the retention duration (UTC) and any auto-delete policies that will apply.

2) Forensic sample: we need a small subset of raw logs (IP anonymized, but preserving session IDs and timestamps) from the 08:45–09:30 UTC window. Please provide a manifest and MD5 checksums so we can validate integrity when we receive the bundle.

We understand you may have policy constraints — if there are residency or export restrictions for the raw artifacts, flag them here and propose an alternative (e.g., redacted extracts or analysis on a Redwoods-held workspace).

Attachments: a short CSV with the session IDs we initially flagged (incident_session_ids.csv).

Appreciate a reply today if possible — our auditors are asking for a preliminary statement.

— Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Security Operations, Valora AI
alex.mercer@valora.ai
+1 415-555-0182
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Valora — post-incident log window and sample request

Evelyn / Marissa — forwarding Valora's ask. TL;DR: they need (a) explicit retention window for affected stacks and (b) a small MD5-signed sample bundle for 08:45–09:30 UTC.

Notes / constraints to consider:
- Valora is an enterprise customer in us-west; they likely require logs to remain available for 90 days per contract but the question is about raw payloads and kernel-level logs which our default retention policy truncates after 30 days unless a hold is applied.
- Residency: I think these logs live in the us-west-2 cluster; we need to confirm export rules (can we deliver an encrypted bundle to their S3, or do we need to stage in our GDrive workspace and share a signed URL?).
- Chain of custody: they requested MD5 checksums. We should produce a manifest csv and a PGP-signed note for integrity, plus logs of who accessed/packaged the bundle.

Can you propose the minimal safe workflow (redaction + hold duration + delivery channel) and flag any approval needed from legal or privacy? They want a reply today.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops-ops@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Valora — post-incident log window and sample request

Jonas / Marissa — thanks for the heads-up. Proposed response and ops plan below (I will own execution if you OK):

1) Retention window:
- For routing/ingress service logs (application-level requests and headers): we will apply a 90-day hold starting 2026-08-30T16:00:00Z (end of our incident window) to align with their contract. After 90 days those logs will be auto-scheduled for deletion by the retention job.
- For low-level host/kernel traces and raw coredumps: policy is 30 days by default. We can create a targeted 60-day hold for the specific session IDs they provided (manifest attached) to balance forensics needs vs storage.

2) Forensic sample packaging:
- We'll produce an encrypted bundle containing anonymized request payloads (IP addresses redacted to RFC 8785 pseudonymization, session IDs preserved), packaged with a manifest (incident_log_manifest.csv) and per-file SHA256 & MD5 checksums.
- Delivery options: (A) scp to Valora's S3 signed upload endpoint (preferred), (B) place the bundle on a pre-authorized Google Drive folder and share a time-limited signed link (if S3 not possible). Note: cross-region export is allowed for this customer (contracted), but legal must sign off if the bundle includes any raw PII beyond IPs.

3) Chain-of-custody:
- I'll generate a custody log and PGP-signed statement with packager identity. All packaging actions will be in the 'forensics' track in our internal ticketing (linked).

Attachments: incident_log_manifest.csv (stub), packing_checklist.md (internal).

Action items: Evelyn to prepare bundle and custody statement; Marissa to confirm S3 endpoint and legal sign-off for export of redacted artifacts.

If we want to be conservative, we can provide the bundle in the Redwoods workspace and offer a remote session to walk their team through forensics instead of transferring raw archives.

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@valora.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Valora — post-incident log window and sample request

Jonas / Evelyn — this plan looks good, thanks. Couple of quick clarifications before you proceed: 

- Can you confirm the exact UTC timestamp when the 90-day hold begins for application logs? Your note said 2026-08-30T16:00:00Z — we want that in writing so our compliance team can close the ticket.
- For the sample bundle: MD5 is fine; SHA256 would be appreciated as well. Can you include both in the manifest?
- If you choose the drive link option, please make it a read-only, expiring link and include the MD5/SHA256 for the archive.

If you can send the manifest and at least one checksum before end of day we'll mark this as 'prelim resolved' on our side.

Thanks,
— Alex
